chunks: And everything in it (the book) that is narrated from Bazi' Al-Mu'adhdhin, I have transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Al-Husayn Al-Sa'dabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Bazi' Al-Mu'adhdhin.

key_terms.السَّعْدَآبَادِيِّ: Al-Sa'dabadi, a nisba indicating origin or residence, attached to Ali ibn Al-Husayn
key_terms.بُزَيْعٍ الْمُؤَذِّنِ: Bazi' Al-Mu'adhdhin, a specific narrator known by his role as a caller to prayer
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ: Muhammad ibn Sinan, a prominent narrator often linked with Bazi'
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُوسَى بْنِ الْمُتَوَكَّل: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil, a key link in this specific transmission chain

ai.seo_question: What is the specific transmission chain for narrations from Bazi' Al-Mu'adhdhin in this text?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies the specific isnad for narrations from Bazi' Al-Mu'adhdhin, tracing them through Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil rather than the more common chain via Muhammad ibn Sinan. This distinction highlights the meticulous attention to transmission accuracy in Shia hadith scholarship, ensuring that each narration is correctly attributed to its primary source within the scholarly network.
